active_paradigms.idea: Exploit affine invariance: fix hull as a regular polygon and use exact LP-based lower-bound structure with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) on the soft-min objective
active_paradigms.description: The score min_area/hull_area is affine-invariant, so we can pin the convex hull to a fixed shape (e.g., regular 13-gon or a triangle) and optimize only interior degrees of freedom. Fixing hull vertices removes the coupling between hull area and triangle areas that makes the ratio objective noisy. Formulate the objective as a smooth soft-min over the 286 triangle areas (LogSumExp with beta ~ 500-2000) divided by the constant hull area, and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' or 'trust-constr' with analytic gradients computed via numpy autodiff-by-hand (the determinant formula is polynomial, so gradients are exact and cheap). Do multi-start from structured seeds: 12-gon + center, 9+3+1 double ring, 13-gon. After convergence, increase beta (continuation) and re-run to sharpen the min. This replaces the current stochastic annealing with a true gradient-based local optimizer that converges to high-precision local optima, which annealing's pattern search cannot reach.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via precise convergence to local optima of the soft-min surrogate
active_paradigms.cautions: The soft-min gradient must be computed exactly (sum of exp weights times triangle-area gradients); beta continuation must be gradual to avoid the optimizer jumping between active triangles; verify final score with the hard min since soft-min slightly underestimates it.

active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-reduced parametric search over 3-fold rotationally symmetric configurations with analytical hull on an ellipse
active_paradigms.description: Known good Heilbronn configurations for n near 13 often exhibit 3-fold rotational symmetry (e.g., points on 3 rotated arcs/rings). Parameterize the configuration with only a handful of variables: 3 orbits under 120-degree rotation, e.g., orbit sizes (4,4,4)+center or (6,6,1), where each orbit is described by 2-4 parameters (radius profile, angular offsets, radial modulation). Since the score is affine-invariant, place orbits on concentric circles. Then exhaustively/grid search this low-dimensional parameter space (5-8 dims) with a dense deterministic grid plus local refinement, evaluating the exact 286-triangle min via the existing vectorized numpy code. Because symmetry collapses the 26-dim search to <10 dims, a grid of even millions of configurations is feasible in seconds, and symmetric configurations automatically avoid near-collinear degeneracies among symmetric triples. This is a structural/combinatorial search rather than continuous optimization, exploring a fundamentally different region of configuration space than unconstrained annealing.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized by exploiting symmetry to search configuration space near-exhaustively
active_paradigms.cautions: Not all symmetric configurations beat asymmetric ones; include several orbit-size partitions (3+3+3+3+1, 4+4+4+1, 6+6+1, 4+4+5) and also reflection-symmetric families; ensure the hull area computation handles points that end up interior (hull is the outer orbit's convex hull, cheap to compute analytically for a regular-ish outer ring).

active_paradigms.idea: Direct maximin nonsmooth optimization via subgradient/active-set iterations on the exact min objective
active_paradigms.description: The hard objective min(a_i)/hull is piecewise-smooth: at any point only a few triangles are active (at the optimum typically 3-6 triangles attain the min). Implement an active-set method: identify the set A of triangles within epsilon of the current minimum, compute the gradient of the objective restricted to moving all 13 points simultaneously (the ratio's gradient w.r.t. all 26 coordinates), take a line-search step along the averaged subgradient direction, update the active set, and shrink the step geometrically on failure. This is the classic maximin (Chebyshev) approach used in facility location and converges to KKT points of the exact nonsmooth problem, unlike soft-min surrogates which never exactly maximize the min. Use scipy.optimize.linprog at each iteration to compute the steepest-ascent direction of the min of linearized triangle areas (a small LP with 26 variables and |A| constraints), guaranteeing a valid ascent direction even with many active triangles. Multi-start from the current best program's output plus structured seeds.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: exact min triangle area (hard objective), avoiding surrogate bias
active_paradigms.cautions: Triangle areas involve absolute values; fix the sign per triangle based on current orientation and re-check after each step (flip signs if orientation changed). Handle hull-area gradient too (piecewise linear in hull vertices) or fix hull vertices as parameters of a fixed regular polygon to simplify. Step sizes must shrink adaptively; validate improvement with the true evaluator formula after each accepted step.
